Holy Trinity Cathedral (Sameba)

The vast Sameba cathedral on Elia Hill — Georgia's largest church and the city's second landmark after Narikala.

Time needed
1 h
From Tbilisi
5 km · 0:15
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Entry
free

Sameba is modern Tbilisi's boldest architectural statement. Built between 1995 and 2004 as a symbol of post-Soviet religious revival, it rises about a hundred metres from floor to the top of its cross, making it one of the tallest Orthodox churches in the South Caucasus.

The architect, Archil Mindiashvili, took the classic Georgian cross-dome plan and scaled it up enormously. The result divides opinion — critics call it too new, too smooth — but the interior genuinely feels different from an old church. Light drops straight from the dome into an almost empty volume, and the sheer emptiness is the point.

The complex is more than one building:

  • The main cathedral with nine chapels, three of them underground
  • A free-standing bell tower, the Patriarch's residence, a seminary and a working monastery
  • Terraced gardens where the Old Town and the roofs of Avlabari line up in a single frame
  • A view that is at its best in the evening, when the cathedral itself is lit

It is worth remembering that Sameba is an active cathedral rather than a monument. You can enter during the liturgy, but wandering with a camera during a service is not welcome, and Sunday mornings are busy with local worshippers rather than visitors.

Practical advice

The dress code is enforced. Women need a headscarf and a skirt below the knee — wraps are handed out free at the entrance — and men need long trousers; shorts will not get you in. Photography inside is often prohibited, so keep the phone away unless you see others using one. Mornings and evenings are best; the terrace has no shade at midday. An hour is enough for the church and the gardens. Toilets are on site, cafés are near Avlabari metro.

How to get there from Tbilisi

The cathedral stands in Avlabari on Elia Hill, ten to fifteen minutes from the centre. Follow signs from either the Metekhi or the Baratashvili bridge — the building is visible from almost everywhere, so getting lost is difficult. There is free parking at the lower gate of the compound, though it fills quickly on feast days; the side streets around Avlabari Square are the fallback. The approach is fully paved with a gentle climb, so any car category is fine. The nearest convenient fuel stations are on Ketevan Dedopali Avenue.
